THE IDEA

Precision that holds through motion.

Loco-manipulation asks more of a humanoid than reproducing a motion. Its hands must reach the right place, its feet must preserve support, and that accuracy must survive changes in posture and movement.

Anchor-0 follows sparse targets from human motion without online retargeting. Curated robot references guide whole-body coordination during training, while feedback corrects execution errors without changing the intended motion representation.

SIMULATION RESULTS

A closer look at control.

One evaluation snapshot, shown together. Hover, tap, or focus a mark for exact values; select a controller in the shared legend to follow it across experiments.

G / L denote reference-input modes, independently of the scoring frame. Motion success requires sustained tracking: wrist and ankle position errors ≤10 cm, orientation errors ≤1 rad, and other body-position errors ≤25 cm. Mean errors use frames before the first 25 cm body-position failure.

Reachability uses robot-space references and requires successful global tracking with no slips, unwanted steps, or touchdowns. All interactive simulation panels use the same test134 / 46k snapshot; the robot demo retains its original published model.

VISION · LANGUAGE · ACTION

Everyday tasks, whole-body solutions.

Time progresses from left to right →

A vision-language-action policy predicts sparse body-part targets and hand commands. Anchor-0 executes the whole-body references in a closed loop. The architecture also supports a motion-token interface through reconstructed near-term targets.

Autonomous task success by interface＋

DISCUSSION

Reliable manipulation starts with reliable control.

Precision, stable support, and predictable motion completion are complementary requirements. The benchmark makes these demands visible, while sparse references and feedback-decoupled control provide a common foundation for teleoperation and autonomous policies.

05

METHOD

Intent stays separate from correction.

Human motion specifies the targets. Curated robot motion guides coordination. Explicit error feedback supports precise execution.

01 /

Sparse commands

Target poses for the pelvis, wrists, and ankles preserve freedom for the rest of the body to coordinate.

02 /

Curated coordination

Paired robot references, produced offline, guide physically plausible and stable motion completion during training.

03 /

Decoupled feedback

Keep execution errors out of motion encoding. Reconstruct targets so the decoder can correct errors under either interface.

Human-motion input representation＋
